newsitem.title: POLAND: Zloty closes firmer, seen heading for parity.
newsitem.headline: Zloty closes firmer, seen heading for parity.

text.p: The zloty strenghtened by half a point on Monday after the National Bank of Poland raised its two official rates by two and 2.5 point to 27 and 24.5 percent respectively as of today, dealers said.
They said trade was mainly speculative with foreign investors mostly on the sidelines.
The local unit was expected to balance out between the central bank established support at -1.5 percent from parity and the parity rate, though some said it might firm more.
"The zloty may climb higher if the speculation is strong enough," said Piotr Czyzewski, forex dealer at ING Bank.
The zloty closed at -0.40/-0.48 percent from the trading band centre against Friday's -0.86/-0.94 as a surge caused by an official interest rate increase faded by mid-day.
It closed at 3.4650/00 to the dollar, against 3.4650/70 on Friday and at 1.8545/55 to the mark, against 1.8713/23.
The central bank increased its lombard rate by two points to 27 percent and its discount by 2.5 points to 24.5 percent.

Dealers expected foreign speculative capital to return to Poland shortly and longer-term foreign inflows to follow if the co-rulling ex-communists continued to lead in public opinion polls in the run-up to parliamentary elections on September 21.
"More and more foreigners will return to Poland over the next four weeks if the ex-communists lead in opinion polls," said Marcin Dec, dealer at Bank Gdanski SA.

The CBOS institute said in a survey on Monday that the recent flood crisis was unlikely to seriously hurt the election chances of the ex-communist SLD, whose familiarity and good track record appeals to many foreign analysts.
Dealers said the zloty's gains were also capped by a strong U.S. dollar, which rose to eight-year highs above 1.87 marks.
One-day rates slipped slightly on Monday as the market was cash-heavy despite the interest rate increase, dealers said.

Overnight rates closed at 24.10/24.60 percent against 24.20/24.55 percent at opening and 24.15/24.55 percent on Friday. Tomorrow/next were at 24.50/24.70 percent, slightly lower from opening's 24.80/24.90.
At Monday's auction the finance ministry sold T-bills worth of 427 million zlotys on investor demand of 832 million.
All average yields rose at the tender with the benchmark 52-week bill yield up to 22.42 percent from last week's 22.24.
